prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1339; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a collision at an intersection while turning left. The claimant, represented by counsel, was the other party's passenger and reported neck pain at the scene.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy declarations and confirmed the driver is named on the policy and the coverage was in force on the reported loss date.

Entry 3: Police report obtained. Responding officers and a witness statement confirm the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time of impact.

Entry 4: Photographs submitted by the insured show the damage to the front quarter panel and bumper, which fits the described impact angle and speed.

Entry 5: Spoke with the appraiser, who reports no earlier damage to the vehicle is on file and nothing indicates the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 6: No independent witnesses have come forward beyond the officer's observations and the statement already on file. Photos confirm some scene details but not the full sequence.

Entry 7: Medical records received from the claimant's provider. The diagnosis of whiplash and the reported symptoms are consistent with the force of a collision of this type.

Entry 8: Counsel's demand package references a prior neck strain several years ago. Records show it was minor, in the same general area, and healed completely with no lasting complaints.

Entry 9: Treatment followed a typical course of physical therapy and medication. Billing and notes show visit frequency tapering as the claimant's range of motion and pain improved.

Entry 10: Claimant's recorded statement, taken through counsel, adds a few minor details about seating position and the moment of braking. The core account of the collision has not changed from the initial report.

Entry 11: Reviewed the medical timeline against the vehicle damage and the account. The injury, treatment pattern, and vehicle damage all line up with the reported loss.

Entry 12: File summary prepared for the supervisor. Liability and coverage are straightforward, and the claimed injury appears consistent with the documented impact. Next step is to evaluate the settlement demand from counsel.
